lead: Missouri plumbing deals with hard water, river flooding and cold snaps. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers from St. Louis to Kansas City.
risk: hard water scale, flooded basements and frozen pipes
risk_short: hard water, flooding and frozen pipes
why: Missouri water is often hard, scaling up water heaters and fixtures. Older homes in St. Louis and Kansas City have cast-iron drains and old sewer laterals.

Heavy rain and river flooding back up sewers and fill basements. Winters freeze pipes. Missouri has no statewide plumber license; cities and counties such as St. Louis and Kansas City license plumbers.
problems: St. Louis, Kansas City and river towns
tips: Test your sump pump before spring.
areas: Calls come from Kansas City, St. Louis, Springfield, Columbia, Independence, Lee's Summit and rural Missouri.

faq.q: Do plumbers need a license in Missouri?
faq.a: Missouri does not license plumbers at the state level. Kansas City, St. Louis, Springfield and many counties run their own licensing and permit programs, so ask your local building office what applies.
